title: Risk of Rain 2-inspired rhythm shooter built with AI. Too similar?
author: Insomnium_111
selftext:
I've been working on a third-person sci-fi shooter using AI, with Risk of Rain 2 being one of the main inspirations.

The twist is that it's also a rhythm game. Shooting, hitting targets, and killing enemies all have beats tied to the music, so combat is meant to feel like you're playing along with the soundtrack.

Still pretty early in development, and I've been experimenting with movement, enemies, combat, and visual effects.

Curious what everyone thinks from the gameplay. Does it look too much like Risk of Rain 2, or does the rhythm-based combat make it different enough?

Does it actually look fun to play? Anything you'd change or improve?

Going to have both stages and endless mode.

Open to criticism and suggestions!

comments.author: xavium
comments.body:
I think it's a good start, you've got a lot to like and experiment with, but it's definitely feeling like more of a risk of rain clone than being inspired. I'd try and find some sort of design direction/style and follow it, keep going until it's way more unique and your own thing. I don't feel like the rhythm part cuts it for me, it just feels like a soundtrack with a repetitive shooting noise (sorry but please add some variance to that lol). 

Keep experimenting and trying new mechanics and things! Visual is always more satisfying to see changes but the real gameplay mechanics are the bits you can test how they actually feel as a player and feedback to ai on and iterate at speed - get it to create toggles and sliders so you can try lots of mechanics in one go, and when something feels nice, polish it and then do some more.

replies.author: Insomnium_111
replies.body:
I appreciate the feedback. Yeah, I was thinking too similar to RoR with looks but different mechanics on it.  
This was pretty much after first prompt with few issues had to fix. 

There’s different rhythms on different stages but still the same shooting noises. I will see if I can change things up a bit make it less repetitive.
